name: Grape wine (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Grape wine [Beverages] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: 22397579, 22397579; USDA (con), 22397579; USDA(con), DTU, MANUAL, Ough, CS. (1984) Volatile nitrogen compounds in fermented beverages. In: Nykänen, L. & Lehtonen, P., eds, Flavour Research of Alcoholic Beverages, Vol. 3, Instrumental and Sensory Analysis, Helsinki, Foundation for Biotechnical and Industrial Fermentation Research, pp. 199-225, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources are ethanol (~105 g/L) then glycerol (~10.5 g/L); dominant organic acid is tartaric (~2.7 g/L) with malic/succinic/lactic/succinic and acetic secondary. The FooDB record was missing every major wine organic acid (tartaric, malic, succinic, lactic, acetic, citric) - the key curation gain here. Residual sugars are low (dry wine, ~6 g/L total, fructose>glucose). Proline is the dominant free amino acid. Values are for a dry red table wine (USDA FDC 173190); white/sweet
curation_added: D-glucose and D-fructose split with amounts
quantified USDA vitamin and mineral panel

curation_removed.name: Cholesterol
curation_removed.reason: Animal sterol; biologically implausible in a grape/yeast fermentation product. FooDB predicted, not measured. USDA reports 0 mg cholesterol in wine.

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: Preformed (animal) vitamin A; absent in wine. USDA reports 0 vitamin A activity. FooDB grape-carryover artifact.

curation_removed.name: Beta-Carotene
curation_removed.reason: Grape-skin carotenoid essentially absent in finished wine (USDA vitamin A ~0); FooDB grape-derived prediction, not a growth nutrient of wine.

curation_removed.name: Lutein
curation_removed.reason: Grape carotenoid negligible in finished wine; FooDB grape-carryover, not a measured wine nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Phytomenadione
curation_removed.reason: Vitamin K1; USDA reports ~0 vitamin K in wine. FooDB grape-carryover, negligible.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+)
curation_removed.reason: Redundant duplicate speciation of iron; consolidated into single 'iron' entry (USDA Fe 0.46 mg/100 g).

curation_removed.name: Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: Compartment-tagged duplicate of iron from a model namespace; not a distinct wine nutrient.

curation_removed.name: O2 O2
curation_removed.reason: Dissolved oxygen is near-zero in finished/bottled wine (reductive storage); not a defining medium component.

basis: per 100 g (~100 mL; finished dry red table wine, wine density ~0.99 g/mL). concentration_mM computed on a per-litre basis.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
